chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadah, from 'Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about forgetfulness (sahw) and what requires the two prostrations of forgetfulness, so he said: 'When you intend to sit but stand up, or intend to stand but sit down, or intend to recite but glorify (God), or intend to glorify but recite, then upon you are the two prostrations of forgetfulness. And there is no forgetfulness in anything that completes the prayer.'

And regarding a man who intends to sit but stands up, then remembers before offering anything or doing anything, he said: 'There is no two prostrations of forgetfulness upon him until he speaks something.'
And regarding a man who forgets in prayer and forgets to perform the two prostrations of forgetfulness, he said: 'He performs them whenever he remembers.'

And regarding a man who prayed three rak'ahs while thinking they were four, and when he gave the salam he remembered they were three, he said: 'He completes his prayer whenever he remembers, prays one rak'ah, recites the tashahhud, gives salam, and performs the two prostrations of forgetfulness, and his prayer is valid.'
And he was asked about a man who forgets the bowing (ruku') or forgets a prostration, is there upon him a prostration of forgetfulness? He said: 'No, he has completed the prayer.'

And regarding a man who enters with the Imam, and the Imam has prayed one rak'ah or more, and the Imam forgets, what should the man do? He said: 'When the Imam gives salam and performs the two prostrations of forgetfulness, the man who entered with him does not prostrate. And when the Imam stands up, completes his prayer, and gives salam, the man performs the two prostrations of forgetfulness.'

And regarding a man who forgets in his prayer and does not remember that until he prays Fajr, what should he do? He said: 'He does not perform the two prostrations of forgetfulness until the sun rises and its rays disappear.'
And regarding a man who forgot behind the Imam and did not begin the prayer, he said: 'He repeats the prayer, and there is no prayer without beginning (iftitah).'

And regarding a man for whom prayer was obligatory while sitting, and he forgot until he stood up and began the prayer while standing, then remembered, he said: 'He sits and begins the prayer while sitting. And likewise, if prayer was obligatory for him while standing, and he forgot until he began the prayer while sitting, then upon him is to cut off his prayer, stand up, and begin the prayer while standing, and he does not count his beginning while sitting.'

key_terms.السَّهْوُ: Forgetfulness or inadvertent error during prayer
key_terms.الْإِفْتِتَاحُ: The beginning or initiation of the prayer
key_terms.خَلْفَ الْإِمَامِ: Behind the Imam (following in congregational prayer)
key_terms.سَجْدَتَا السَّهْوِ: The two prostrations of forgetfulness performed to compensate for specific errors in prayer
key_terms.يَبْنِي عَلَى صَلَاتِهِ: He completes his prayer (by adding the missing portion)

ai.seo_question: What actions in prayer require the two prostrations of forgetfulness (sajdat al-sahw) according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* delineates the precise conditions for *sajdat al-sahw*, distinguishing between transitional errors that necessitate atonement and simple omissions that do not. It further addresses complex jurisprudential scenarios, such as the follower's obligation when the Imam forgets and the validity of prayer if the error is remembered after the prayer time has expired, reflecting the Shia emphasis on maintaining the structural integrity of worship through corrective acts. The text underscores the principle that minor forgetfulness does not invalidate the prayer, provided the essential pillars are completed, while highlighting the necessity of rectifying significant deviations in posture or sequence.
